_comment: Explicit exceptions to the local clock-gating rules (tools/check-cg.py, docs/rtl-coding-style.md 'Local clock gating'). One entry per module, rule (CG-1, CG-2 or CG-3) and register; why says what was measured and why the rule cannot or should not be met. A waiver that excuses nothing is refused.

waivers.why: A repeater stage exists because its input arrives after a cycle of wire. Any enable that could tell a new valid from a held one has to see that input, and an ICG enable must set up before the flop's own D does, so it would turn a wire-limited path into a gate-limited one. The pulse flops are 3 * SLOTS + 1 a stage, 14 at the unit's parameters; the module's allowance of 7 takes wake_q and credit_q, and this and stall_q remain. The payload, most of the flops, is gated by this flop (pay_en, 0.0 NGD, DCGE 99-100%).
As valid_q: the stall arrives over the link's wire, so an enable that sees it reaches the clock gate late. Past the module's allowance of 7, which wake_q and credit_q fill.

6 flops on their own change-only enable (DCGE 100%), under CCV_CG_MIN_FLOPS, so no clock gate. q_run_q and s_run_q are 12 flops, past the module's allowance of 7, which wake_q and hold_q (3) use. One gate over both counters needs an enable that ORs theirs, past 8 NGD because of the hysteresis compare, or a coarser one whose DCGE falls to about 0% in idle. Registering the compare would make one shallow gate, but a CSR change would then take effect a cycle later than docs/clock-gate.md says: Daniel's call (DA tab, 2026-10-17).
